title: Fabio Wardley activates Daniel Dubois rematch clause: ‘I’m coming for you and my belt’
content:
Fabio Wardley has activated a clause for an immediate rematch with Daniel Dubois following his defeat last weekend in what promoter Frank Warren called “the best heavyweight fight I have ever put on.”

The 31-year-old lost his WBO world heavyweight title to Dubois, who became a two-time heavyweight champion, after a brutal bout which saw referee Howard Foster step in to stop it in the 11th round. While Wardley (20-1-1), was never knocked down, and even had Dubois (23-3-0) down twice in the early rounds (the first time after just 10 seconds), he ended the fight bloodied and bruised, leaving many watching believing the fight should have been stopped earlier.

But less than a week after suffering the first professional loss of his career, promoter Queensberry confirmed in a statement that Wardley had activated the rematch clause that was specified in the contract for their first fight and said: “All parties will now work towards a rematch of their fight of the year contender for later in 2026.”

The deadline by which time that fight has to take place is the end of 2026.

“The boxing world knows my character, and Saturday night proved that without a shred of doubt,” Wardley said in a statement to Sky Sports.

“It was a fight for the ages, but I made some mistakes that I will rectify in the rematch. Congratulations to Daniel, but I’m coming for you and my belt.”

Analysis by Sarah Shephard

I wrote on Monday how uncomfortable watching the later stages of Wardley v Dubois made me, but I started the night incredibly excited about the fight that was to come. Two huge hitters facing off in their prime is the stuff boxing dreams are made of. And the fight absolutely delivered on all that it promised.

Given the title “Don’t Blink” by the promoters, it played out exactly that way, with Wardley knocking Dubois down after just 10 seconds. He had the challenger down again in the third round before Dubois fought his way back into the bout and swung the momentum violently in his direction, landing some of the most destructive jabs you’ll ever see. The doctors twice took a look at Wardley’s face, which was a bloody, swollen mess by the later rounds, but allowed him to continue until the referee finally called a stop to the fight in round 11.

Dubois silenced his critics with an exceptional, resilient performance against Wardley, but the fact he was knocked down twice makes the possibility of a rematch a far tastier one than if he’d been dominant from the start.

Wardley did not need hospital treatment after the fight, but was clearly badly hurt and will need time for his facial injuries to recover, not to mention the damage that was not visible on the night. Many wanted to see Wardley out of action for the rest of the year, but he will want to try and put right his wrongs as early as possible, which means going straight back into the fire. Hopefully those around him will ensure he takes as long a break as possible before returning to training in time for Wardley v Dubois II: A fight that will not need selling after the drama of the first one.
